channel_intelligence.state_of_channel: Day 42. 11 subscribers (+1), 61 public videos (+15), 3,829 lifetime views (2,798 -> 3,829, +37%). Studio 28-day: 3,768 views (+40% WoW), 125.7 watch hours (+17.7%), 14,970 impressions at 2.8% CTR. The single most important thing this week is not a number, it is a discovery: after three weeks of being locked out, the CTR / impressions / traffic-source data finally came out of Studio Advanced mode, and it rewrites the strategy. SUGGESTED VIDEOS delivers 82.9% of all channel watch time (104.2 of 125.7 hours) from only 10.8% of views, at 15:25 average view duration and 3.6% CTR. YOUTUBE SEARCH, the thing every long title has been engineered for, served 4,586 impressions and converted 0.9% of them into 136 views - and not one of the top search queries is a Study/Focus/Work/Sleep term. The Shorts feed supplies 81.5% of views but 1.6% of watch time. Meanwhile the biggest watch-time asset on the channel is a Fun Bossa long: 'Happy Bossa Nova Lounge' banked 30.1 hours - 24% of everything - from just 81 views, at 4.7% CTR. Social is compounding hard: Instagram jumped 9 -> 27 followers (+200%) and overtook TikTok (20 -> 32) as the fastest grower, on 42 posts out this week with zero failures.
what_works: SUGGESTED VIDEOS IS THE REAL ENGINE, NOT SEARCH: 405 views (10.8%) produced 104.2 watch hours (82.9% of the channel) at 15:25 AVD and 3.6% CTR. Search produced 4,586 impressions, 0.9% CTR, 136 views, 4.4 hours. Every hour of watch time the channel has is coming from YouTube deciding to recommend a long next to another long.

FUN BOSSA LONGS BEAT SOFT BOSSA ON WATCH TIME, 2.3x: Fun longs average 18.8 watch hours per video at 4.78% impression-weighted CTR; Soft longs average 8.3 hours at 3.46%. 'Happy Bossa Nova Lounge' alone is 30.1 hours (24% of channel watch time) from 81 views. Views alone had the two styles tied (39.8 vs 38.0) - watch time separates them. Caveat: Fun n=2, and the winner runs 1:39:06 vs Soft's 1:17:43, so length is part of the edge.

THE CAPTION RANKING IS SOLID, THE TOP NUMBER IS NOT: 'A minute of calm for your day' averages 169 views over 4 posts with no outlier (max 276 of 676 total) - the best-evidenced caption on the channel. 'Bossa nova + coffee = perfect morning' shows avg 330 over 4, but 1,031 of its 1,318 views are one post; strip that and it averages 95.7. The bottom caption, 'Soft jazz to ease into the day', averages 19 over 5 posts - so the honest gap top-to-bottom is 5x, not 17x. Still decisive. Winners name a SENSORY PAIR or address the viewer's day; losers describe the music.

NOON BEATS 6PM FOR REELS, 2.6x: the 16:00Z slot averages 128.1 views across 18 reels; the 22:00Z slot averages 49.5 across 17. Strip the 1,031 outlier and noon still leads 74.9 to 49.5. By day, Saturday (150.5, n=4) and Thursday (88.2, n=6) beat Monday/Tuesday/Wednesday (31-44, n=4-5) - directional at these sample sizes, not settled.

PLAYLISTS LOOK LIKE THE BEST-CONVERTING SURFACE: 6.9% CTR and 13:25 AVD, roughly double suggested-video CTR - but on only 216 impressions and 23 views, so this is a hypothesis worth testing cheaply, not an established fact. The point stands that the channel has barely used the placement at all.
next_moves: STOP OPTIMIZING LONG TITLES FOR SEARCH; OPTIMIZE FOR SUGGESTED. Search returns 0.9% CTR and no study/focus queries at all. Suggested returns 82.9% of watch time. That means titles and thumbnails should be built to look like the NEXT video in a session next to the videos already winning - same visual family, same mood language - not stuffed with 'Study Music for Focus & Concentration'. Test this on the next two Monday longs and compare CTR.

TEST FUN BOSSA AT ~100 MINUTES ON THE NEXT TWO LONGS. Fun carries 2.3x the watch hours per video and higher CTR, but on n=2, and 30.1 of its 37.6 hours is a single video that also happens to be the longest on the channel (1:39:06 vs Soft's 1:17:43). So this is a two-video test, not a settled rule - run it, because it costs nothing in the render queue, and re-check next week before committing the rotation.

REBUILD THE THUMBNAIL ON 'Cozy Coffee Shop Bossa Nova - Study Music'. It has the most impressions on the channel by far (2,020) and the worst CTR of the majors (2.9%). Moving it to the 4.0-4.7% range the other high-impression longs achieve is worth roughly 25-40 extra views a month from work already done. (Ignore the 10.4% and 8.9% CTR outliers as benchmarks - those are 125 and 79 impressions, too small to aim at.)

BUILD AND FILL PLAYLISTS - cheap test, potentially large payoff. Playlists show 6.9% CTR and 13:25 AVD but on only 216 impressions, so the signal is thin. Group the longs into 2-3 themed playlists (Morning Cafe, Deep Focus, Sleep) and add every long to one. Costs an hour, and it feeds the suggested-video engine that already produces 83% of watch time.
CUT 'Soft jazz to ease into the day' FROM THE CAPTION BANK (avg 19 over 5 posts) and weight the reel batch toward the two proven captions. Move the reel schedule to favour the noon slot and Thu/Sat.

UNBLOCK THE ANALYTICS API - it is two fixes, not one. (1) Enable the YouTube Analytics API in Google Cloud project 16378841695 (it returns 403 SERVICE_DISABLED - it has never been turned on; prior reports only knew about the scope problem). (2) Re-run the OAuth consent with yt-analytics.readonly added. Do both and this whole report automates instead of needing Chrome.

channel_intelligence.suno_rules: Data-backed prompt rules: (1) always 'instrumental / no vocals' - this is background music; (2) keep energy CONSISTENT with no dynamic spikes - listeners on 15-minute suggested-video sessions leave when a track jumps; (3) WRITE LONGER SETS - the channel's #1 watch-time video runs 1:39:06 and banks 30.1 hours from 81 views; target ~100 minutes of continuous material per long, not 77; (4) TEST FUN/UPBEAT BOSSA over soft/sleepy for longs - Fun Bossa shows 2.3x the watch hours per video (18.8 vs 8.3) and higher impression-weighted CTR (4.78% vs 3.46%), but on only 2 videos, one of which supplies 30.1 of the 37.6 hours - treat as a live test on the next two longs, not a settled rule; (5) name 2-3 concrete instruments, not just a genre; (6) NEW, IMPORTANT - stop engineering longs around Study/Focus/Work SEARCH keywords. Search converted 4,586 impressions at 0.9% into 136 views, and zero top queries were study/focus terms. 82.9% of watch time comes from SUGGESTED VIDEOS, so the music and packaging should aim to be the natural next track in an existing session: same mood family, same tempo range, same cafe world as what is already getting recommended; (7) reels and longs stay on separate title systems - longs get mood/session language, reels get casual feeling captions ('A minute of calm for your day' avg 169 over 4 with no outlier is the best-evidenced; 'Bossa nova + coffee = perfect morning' avg 330 but 95.7 excluding its single 1,031 breakout; 'Soft jazz to ease into the day' avg 19 is retired - a 5x honest gap top to bottom); (8) reel captions that name a SENSORY PAIR or speak to the viewer's day beat captions that describe the music.

deep_analytics.source: YouTube Studio Advanced mode explore table (ADM account in Chrome), 2026-08-03
deep_analytics.avg_view_duration: 8:10 channel average as displayed by Studio - NOTE this does not reconcile (125.7 hrs / 3,768 views = 2:00). Studio's AVD column is unreliable on the aggregate and Shorts-feed rows, almost certainly a Shorts watch-time accounting artifact. The Suggested (15:25), Playlists (13:25) and Browse (10:44) rows DO reconcile and are trustworthy; reels 0:05-0:15 (8-25% viewed) come from the per-video table and are trustworthy.

top_traffic_sources.caveat: 0.9% of 4,586 = 41 clicks but 136 views attributed; every other source sits at a 1.0-1.6x views-to-clicks ratio. The direction (search converts far below every other surface) is safe; the exact 0.9% needs re-capture.

deep_analytics.key_read: Suggested videos, not search, is where the channel lives: 10.8% of views produce 82.9% of watch time. Search is a dead end at 0.9% CTR with no study/focus queries in the top list. Reels dominate view count (81.5%) but contribute 1.6% of watch time, so they are a reach and subscriber-funnel instrument only. Longs - especially Fun Bossa longs near 100 minutes - are the entire watch-time business.
deep_analytics.method_note: Captured by coordinate-clicking the 'Advanced mode' button in Studio (top-right) - the tab-reach_viewers deep-link and the Content tab a11y click both fail. Breakdown selector on the left switches Content -> Traffic source, and clicking a traffic source row drills into search terms.
deep_analytics.still_pending: Analytics API automation. Two blockers: YouTube Analytics API is disabled in Google Cloud project 16378841695 (403 SERVICE_DISABLED), and token.json lacks the yt-analytics.readonly scope. Thumbnail font per video is still unlogged by make_thumbnail.py.

social_intelligence.state_of_socials: Followers: Instagram 27 (+18, from 9 - up 200%), TikTok 32 (+12, from 20), YouTube 11 (+1). Instagram has taken over as the fastest-growing platform after three weeks as the laggard, nearly tripling in a week. Cadence is up and clean: 42 posts went out in the trailing 7 days (14 each on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts), up from 33, with every single post reporting status=published and zero failures. The SSD clip queue sits at 102 - flat versus last week, meaning the nightly batch is replacing exactly what gets posted, so there is no supply risk but also no headroom to raise cadence without raising batch output. The single most important thing: the reel engine is accelerating rather than resting on the Jul 24 breakout. Two reels posted on Aug 1 pulled 263 and 224 views inside 48 hours, and YouTube realtime shows 510 views in the last 48 hours. But the funnel has a hard truth attached - YouTube's External traffic source recorded just 4 views in 28 days, so the social accounts are growing their own audiences and feeding the Shorts feed, not driving click-through to the YouTube channel.
whats_out: 42 reels live in the last 7d across Instagram (14), TikTok (14), YouTube Shorts (14) - full 2x/day cadence at 12:00 and 18:00 ET, zero failed posts

This week's top reels: 'Press play, let the cafe come to you' 263 (Sat 6pm), 'Bossa nova + coffee = perfect morning' 224 (Sat noon), 'Slow down for a minute' 140 (Thu 6pm) and 113 (Mon noon), 'A minute of calm for your day' 111 (Wed noon)
Instagram 9 -> 27 (+200%) overtakes TikTok 20 -> 32 (+60%) as the fastest grower; YouTube 10 -> 11
Clip queue flat at 102 on the SSD - batch output and posting cadence are now exactly in balance

FUNNEL REALITY CHECK: YouTube 'External' traffic = 4 views in 28 days. Reels build audience on-platform via the Shorts feed (81.5% of all channel views) but the bio-link path to the channel is delivering essentially nothing.
suggestions: MOVE THE POSTING WEIGHT TO NOON. The 12:00 ET slot averages 128.1 views across 18 reels versus 49.5 across 17 at 18:00 - a 2.6x gap that holds at 1.5x even after removing the 1,031 outlier. Either shift both daily posts earlier or make noon the slot that gets the strongest caption.

RETIRE 'Soft jazz to ease into the day' (avg 19 views over 5 posts) and any caption that describes the music. Lead with 'A minute of calm for your day' (avg 169 over 4, no outlier - the best-evidenced caption on the channel) and 'Bossa nova + coffee = perfect morning' (avg 330, but 95.7 if you exclude its single 1,031 breakout). Honest top-to-bottom gap is 5x, which is still more than enough to act on. The rule the data supports: name a sensory pair or speak to the viewer's day.

DOUBLE DOWN ON INSTAGRAM. It tripled this week and is now the fastest grower in both absolute and percentage terms. Give it the strongest caption of the day and test Reels-native features (audio, cover frame) there first before rolling changes to TikTok.

WEIGHT THE SCHEDULE TOWARD THU-SAT - directionally, not dogmatically. Saturday averages 150.5 views per reel (n=4) and Thursday 88.2 (n=6), versus 31-44 for Mon/Tue/Wed (n=4-5). Friday's headline average is an artifact of the single 1,031 breakout - stripped out, Friday is the worst day at 18.6. Sample sizes are 4-7 per day, so revisit in two weeks before hard-coding the schedule.
RAISE BATCH OUTPUT BEFORE RAISING CADENCE. The queue is flat at 102, so any increase in posts/day drains it. Bump make_reels_batch.py output first if the plan is to go past 2 posts/day.

STOP COUNTING ON THE BIO LINK AS THE FUNNEL. 4 External views in 28 days says the click-out path does not work. The reels' real value to YouTube is Shorts-feed reach and subscriber growth on-platform - so prioritize captions and hooks that win in-feed over captions that try to send people to the channel.
